definition: Polysemanticity is a phenomenon in neural networks in which individual neurons respond to multiple unrelated concepts rather than to a single well-defined one.
details: A polysemantic neuron might activate for legal text, DNA sequences, and Hebrew script simultaneously. Because such neurons cannot be straightforwardly interpreted, polysemanticity is a central obstacle in mechanistic interpretability.

explainer.lead: Polysemanticity is a core obstacle in mechanistic interpretability: because a single neuron mixes several unrelated concepts, you cannot read the network's behaviour off individual units.

tiers.eli5: Most neurons are like a light switch wired to several rooms at once — flip it and the kitchen, garage and attic all light up.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers trying to explain a model's internals hit polysemantic neurons that resist clean unit-level labels, so they turn to methods that look for directions or features spanning many neurons; assuming one neuron equals one concept is the common pitfall.
tiers.paperLevel: A neuron is polysemantic when its activation responds to multiple unrelated concepts rather than a single well-defined one; such neurons cannot be straightforwardly interpreted.
